title: The Uplift an Employer's Programme Allows for Length of Service on the Account
content:
An Employee Meal Account that has been open a long time before its restriction began carries an uplift on the share the employer's dining programme picks up. The long service term is 24 months, the long service uplift is 5 percent and the short service uplift is 2 percent.

**Clause.** Where the whole months between the day the account was activated and the day its restriction began are more than the long service term and three or more charges have been accrued on the account in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, that uplift is the long service uplift. Where those whole months are more than the long service term and fewer than three charges have been accrued on the account in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, that uplift is the short service uplift. Where neither holds, the uplift the employer's programme allows for length of service is nothing.

## The bands

| Whole months from activation to the start of the restriction | Charges accrued in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked | Uplift |
|---|---|---|
| More than 24 | 3 or more | 5 percent |
| More than 24 | Fewer than 3, including none | 2 percent |
| 24 or fewer | Any | Nothing |

## Points of judgement

The months counted run from the day the account was activated to the day its restriction began, not to today, and they are counted in whole months; 24 whole months is not more than the long service term, while 25 is.

*Hypothetical illustration.* An account activated 40 whole months before its restriction began, carrying 3 charges in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, takes an uplift of 5 percent; the same account with 1 charge in that month takes 2 percent. An account activated 18 whole months before the restriction began takes no uplift on this ground however it has been charged.
